Apple___Apple_scab.name: Apple Scab
Apple___Apple_scab.summary: A common fungal disease favoured by cool, wet spring weather. It rarely kills trees but blemishes fruit and can defoliate susceptible cultivars.
symptoms: Olive-green to brown velvety spots on leaves, later turning dark and corky
Leaves may curl, yellow and drop early
Scabby, cracked dark lesions on fruit
treatment: Remove and destroy heavily infected leaves and fruit
Apply a registered protectant fungicide (e.g. captan or sulfur) from green tip through petal fall during wet periods
Follow local extension spray schedules and product label directions
prevention: Rake and shred or compost fallen leaves in autumn to reduce overwintering spores
Prune to open the canopy and speed leaf drying

Apple___Black_rot.name: Black Rot
Apple___Black_rot.summary: Causes leaf spots (frogeye leaf spot), fruit rot and limb cankers. The fungus survives in dead wood, cankers and mummified fruit.
symptoms: Small purple spots on leaves that enlarge into tan centres with purple margins (frogeye)
Expanding brown-to-black rot on fruit, often with concentric rings
Sunken reddish-brown cankers on branches
treatment: Prune out dead wood and cankers well below visible symptoms
Remove mummified fruit from the tree and ground
Apply a labelled fungicide during the growing season where disease pressure is high
prevention: Keep trees vigorous with proper fertilisation and watering
Remove prunings and debris from the orchard

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.name: Cedar Apple Rust
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.summary: A rust fungus that alternates between apple and eastern red cedar/juniper. Spores from galls on junipers infect apple leaves in spring.
symptoms: Bright yellow-orange spots on the upper leaf surface
Small tube-like structures on the underside of spots later in the season
Premature leaf drop and lesions on fruit in severe cases
treatment: Apply a labelled rust fungicide (e.g. myclobutanil) from pink bud until about a month after bloom
Remove heavily infected leaves where practical
prevention: Remove nearby juniper/red cedar hosts or their galls where feasible
Monitor junipers for orange gelatinous galls in wet spring weather

Apple___healthy.name: Healthy
Apple___healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected. The leaf looks healthy.
prevention: Keep scouting regularly, especially after wet weather
Maintain good canopy airflow through pruning
Clean up fallen leaves and fruit in autumn

Background_without_leaves.name: No leaf detected
Background_without_leaves.summary: The image does not appear to contain a plant leaf. Try a close-up photo of a single leaf on a plain background.
prevention: Fill most of the frame with one leaf
Use even daylight and avoid harsh shadows
Hold the camera steady to avoid blur

Blueberry___healthy.name: Healthy
Blueberry___healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected. The leaf looks healthy.
prevention: Prune old canes to improve airflow

Cherry___Powdery_mildew.name: Powdery Mildew
Cherry___Powdery_mildew.summary: A fungal disease that thrives in warm days, cool nights and high humidity. It weakens trees and can damage fruit quality.
symptoms: White powdery patches on young leaves, often on the underside first
Leaves curl upward and may become distorted or brittle
Powdery growth on fruit and shoots in severe infections
treatment: Apply sulfur, potassium bicarbonate or another labelled fungicide at first sign of infection
Remove heavily infected shoots
prevention: Prune for an open canopy and good air circulation
Avoid excessive nitrogen fertiliser, which drives susceptible soft growth
Control root suckers and water sprouts

Cherry___healthy.name: Healthy
Cherry___healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected. The leaf looks healthy.
prevention: Scout new growth for mildew in humid weather
Prune to keep the canopy open

Corn___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray_leaf_sp.name: Gray Leaf Spot
Corn___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray_leaf_sp.summary: One of the most yield-limiting foliar diseases of corn, favoured by warm, humid weather and corn residue left on the surface.
symptoms: Rectangular tan to grey lesions bounded by leaf veins
Lesions may merge, blighting large areas of the leaf
Symptoms usually start on lower leaves
treatment: Apply a labelled foliar fungicide around tasselling if disease is present on upper leaves of susceptible hybrids
Base spray decisions on scouting and local thresholds
prevention: Rotate away from corn for at least one year
Bury or manage infected residue with tillage where appropriate

Corn___Common_rust.name: Common Rust
Corn___Common_rust.summary: A rust disease spread by wind-blown spores, favoured by cool temperatures and high humidity.
symptoms: Small, elongated cinnamon-brown pustules on both leaf surfaces
Pustules rupture and release powdery rust-coloured spores
Heavy infection causes leaf yellowing and dieback
treatment: Apply a labelled fungicide early if infection is severe on susceptible hybrids before tasselling
Most field corn hybrids tolerate rust without spraying
prevention: Plant early to avoid peak spore periods
Scout regularly during cool, humid weather

Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.name: Northern Leaf Blight
Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.summary: A foliar disease favoured by moderate temperatures and long periods of leaf wetness. Severe infection before silking can cause major yield loss.
symptoms: Long, cigar-shaped grey-green to tan lesions (2.5 to 15 cm)
Lesions develop dark spore masses in humid weather
Starts on lower leaves and moves upward
treatment: Apply a labelled foliar fungicide around tasselling to silking when lesions are present on upper leaves
Scout fields with susceptible hybrids closely
prevention: Rotate crops and manage corn residue
Avoid continuous corn in high-risk fields

Corn___healthy.name: Healthy
Corn___healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected. The leaf looks healthy.
prevention: Rotate crops to break disease cycles
Choose hybrids with good foliar disease ratings
Scout lower leaves during humid weather

Grape___Black_rot.name: Black Rot
Grape___Black_rot.summary: A serious disease in warm, humid climates that can destroy most of a crop. It overwinters in mummified berries.
symptoms: Tan to reddish-brown circular leaf spots with dark borders and tiny black dots
Berries turn brown, then shrivel into hard black mummies
Elongated dark lesions on shoots and tendrils
treatment: Remove and destroy mummified berries and infected tissue
Apply labelled fungicides (e.g. mancozeb, myclobutanil) from early shoot growth through about 4 weeks after bloom
prevention: Prune and train vines for good air circulation
Clean up mummies from vines and the ground before bud break
Control weeds to reduce humidity in the canopy

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).name: Esca (Black Measles)
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).pathogen: Phaeomoniella chlamydospora, Phaeoacremonium spp. (trunk disease complex)
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).summary: A grapevine trunk disease caused by wood-infecting fungi that enter through pruning wounds. It can cause sudden vine collapse.
symptoms: 'Tiger-stripe' pattern: yellow or red-brown bands between leaf veins
Small dark spots on berries (measles)
Dark streaking in cross-sections of wood; sudden wilting (apoplexy)
treatment: No curative spray exists; remove and burn severely affected vines or trunks
Retrain new trunks from healthy suckers where possible
prevention: Prune in dry weather and protect large pruning wounds with a sealant or labelled wound protectant
Delay pruning to late dormancy where practical

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.name: Leaf Blight (Isariopsis Leaf Spot)
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.summary: A leaf spot disease of grapes common in warm, humid regions, usually appearing later in the season.
symptoms: Irregular dark red-brown to black spots on older leaves
Spots merge and leaves may dry and drop early
Dark fungal growth on the underside of lesions
treatment: Remove infected leaves
Apply a labelled protectant fungicide; sprays for other grape diseases often control it too
prevention: Improve canopy ventilation through pruning and shoot positioning

Grape___healthy.name: Healthy
Grape___healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected. The leaf looks healthy.
prevention: Keep the canopy open for airflow
Remove mummified fruit during dormant pruning
Scout leaves weekly in humid weather

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).name: Huanglongbing (Citrus Greening)
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).pathogen: Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus (spread by the Asian citrus psyllid)
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).summary: One of the most destructive citrus diseases worldwide. It is incurable, and infected trees decline and produce bitter, misshapen fruit.
symptoms: Blotchy, asymmetrical yellow mottling of leaves (unlike symmetrical nutrient deficiency)
Small, lopsided fruit that stays green at the bottom
Twig dieback and overall tree decline
treatment: There is no cure; remove confirmed infected trees to protect neighbours
Report suspected cases to your local agriculture authority, as it is regulated in many regions
Nutritional programmes can prolong productivity but do not cure
prevention: Control the Asian citrus psyllid vector
Plant only certified disease-free nursery stock
Inspect trees regularly and do not move citrus plants between regions

Peach___Bacterial_spot.name: Bacterial Spot
Peach___Bacterial_spot.summary: A bacterial disease favoured by warm, wet, windy weather, especially on sandy soils. It causes defoliation and blemished fruit.
symptoms: Small water-soaked spots on leaves that turn purple-brown and angular
Lesion centres fall out, giving a shot-hole appearance
Pitting and cracking spots on fruit
treatment: Apply copper-based bactericides or oxytetracycline per label, typically from shuck split onward
Use lower copper rates after leaf-out to avoid leaf injury
prevention: Site orchards away from strong winds or use windbreaks

Peach___healthy.name: Healthy
Peach___healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected. The leaf looks healthy.
prevention: Choose resistant cultivars where bacterial spot is common
Prune to an open centre for airflow

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.name: Bacterial Spot
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.summary: A seed-borne bacterial disease that spreads by splashing water. Warm, rainy weather can make it explode in a field.
symptoms: Small water-soaked spots on leaves that turn brown with yellow halos
Leaves yellow and drop, exposing fruit to sunscald
Raised, scabby spots on fruit
treatment: Remove severely infected plants
Apply copper-based bactericides, often combined with mancozeb, per label
Avoid working in fields while foliage is wet
prevention: Use certified disease-free or treated seed and transplants
Rotate away from peppers and tomatoes for 2 to 3 years
Use drip irrigation instead of overhead watering

Pepper,_bell___healthy.name: Healthy
Pepper,_bell___healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected. The leaf looks healthy.
prevention: Water at the base to keep leaves dry

Potato___Early_blight.name: Early Blight
Potato___Early_blight.summary: A common fungal disease affecting older leaves first, favoured by alternating wet and dry periods and stressed plants.
symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings (target-board pattern)
Yellow halo around lesions; lower, older leaves affected first
Leaves wither and drop as lesions merge
treatment: Remove infected lower leaves
Apply a labelled fungicide (e.g. chlorothalonil, mancozeb or azoxystrobin) when symptoms first appear
Maintain adequate nitrogen to reduce plant stress
prevention: Rotate with non-solanaceous crops for 2 to 3 years
Avoid overhead irrigation late in the day and destroy volunteer plants

Potato___Late_blight.name: Late Blight
Potato___Late_blight.summary: The disease behind the Irish potato famine. In cool, wet weather it can destroy a whole field within days and rot tubers in storage.
symptoms: Large, dark, water-soaked lesions on leaves, often starting at tips and edges
White fuzzy growth on the leaf underside in humid conditions
Brown, firm rot on tubers
treatment: Act quickly: remove and bag infected plants and do not compost them
Apply a labelled late-blight fungicide (e.g. chlorothalonil, mancozeb, or systemic products like cymoxanil) to protect healthy plants
Kill vines 2 to 3 weeks before harvest to protect tubers
prevention: Plant certified disease-free seed potatoes and resistant varieties
Destroy cull piles and volunteer potatoes
Monitor local late-blight forecasts and alerts

Potato___healthy.name: Healthy
Potato___healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected. The leaf looks healthy.
prevention: Scout often in cool, wet weather for late blight

Raspberry___healthy.name: Healthy
Raspberry___healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected. The leaf looks healthy.

Soybean___healthy.name: Healthy
Soybean___healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected. The leaf looks healthy.
prevention: Choose varieties with good disease resistance packages

Squash___Powdery_mildew.name: Powdery Mildew
Squash___Powdery_mildew.summary: A very common cucurbit disease that does not need wet leaves to infect. It reduces fruit size, quality and storage life.
symptoms: White powdery spots on leaves and stems, starting on older leaves
Spots spread to cover whole leaves
Leaves yellow, brown and die early
treatment: Apply sulfur, potassium bicarbonate, neem/horticultural oil or another labelled fungicide at first symptoms
Alternate fungicide modes of action to prevent resistance
prevention: Space plants for good airflow and full sun

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.name: Leaf Scorch
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.summary: A fungal leaf disease that weakens plants and reduces vigour and yield over time, spreading in wet weather.
symptoms: Many small, irregular purplish spots on the upper leaf surface
Spots merge and the leaf looks scorched or burnt
Leaf edges curl and dry
treatment: Remove and destroy infected leaves after harvest (renovation)
Apply a labelled fungicide during wet periods if disease is severe
prevention: Plant resistant cultivars and certified disease-free plants
Use drip irrigation and good spacing
Renovate beds and remove old foliage annually

Strawberry___healthy.name: Healthy
Strawberry___healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected. The leaf looks healthy.
prevention: Mulch to keep fruit and leaves off the soil

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.name: Bacterial Spot
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.pathogen: Xanthomonas spp. (X. euvesicatoria, X. perforans and others)
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.summary: A seed-borne bacterial disease spread by rain splash and handling, favoured by warm, wet conditions.
symptoms: Small, dark, greasy-looking spots on leaves, sometimes with yellow halos
Spots may merge and leaves turn yellow and drop
Raised, scabby spots on green fruit
treatment: Remove and destroy badly infected plants
Apply copper-based bactericides (often with mancozeb) per label
Avoid handling plants when wet
prevention: Use certified disease-free seed and transplants
Rotate away from tomatoes and peppers for 2 to 3 years
Use drip irrigation and stake plants for airflow

Tomato___Early_blight.name: Early Blight
Tomato___Early_blight.summary: A widespread fungal disease that starts on lower, older leaves and can defoliate plants, exposing fruit to sunscald.
symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings (target pattern) and yellow halos
Lower leaves affected first, then yellow and drop
Dark leathery lesions at the stem end of fruit
treatment: Prune and dispose of infected lower leaves
Apply a labelled fungicide (e.g. chlorothalonil, copper or mancozeb) at first symptoms
prevention: Mulch to stop soil splashing onto leaves
Rotate crops and remove plant debris
Stake or cage plants and water at the base

Tomato___Late_blight.name: Late Blight
Tomato___Late_blight.summary: A fast-moving, highly destructive disease in cool, wet weather. It can kill plants within a week and spreads to nearby potatoes.
symptoms: Large, irregular grey-green to brown water-soaked patches on leaves
White fuzzy growth on the leaf underside in humid weather
Firm, greasy brown blotches on fruit
treatment: Remove and bag infected plants immediately and do not compost them
Protect remaining plants with a labelled late-blight fungicide
Alert nearby growers, since spores travel on the wind
prevention: Do not save seed potatoes or plant from unknown sources
Keep foliage dry and space plants for airflow

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.name: Leaf Mold
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.summary: Mainly a greenhouse and high-tunnel disease, favoured by relative humidity above 85%.
symptoms: Pale green to yellow patches on the upper leaf surface
Olive-green to grey-brown velvety mould on the underside
Leaves wither and drop; older leaves first
treatment: Remove infected leaves
Reduce humidity with ventilation and heating
Apply a labelled fungicide if needed
prevention: Space and prune plants for airflow

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.name: Septoria Leaf Spot
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.summary: One of the most common tomato leaf diseases. It spreads by splashing water and can severely defoliate plants.
symptoms: Many small circular spots with dark borders and grey-white centres
Tiny black specks (fruiting bodies) in the centre of spots
Starts on lower leaves after fruit set
treatment: Remove infected lower leaves promptly
Apply a labelled fungicide (e.g. chlorothalonil or copper) on a regular schedule in wet weather
prevention: Mulch and water at the base
Rotate crops for at least one year and remove debris

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.name: Two-spotted Spider Mite
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.summary: Tiny mites that suck plant cells, thriving in hot, dry, dusty conditions. Populations can build very quickly.
symptoms: Fine yellow or white stippling on leaves
Fine webbing on the underside of leaves and between stems
Leaves bronze, dry and drop in heavy infestations
treatment: Spray the leaf undersides with a strong water jet to knock mites off
Apply insecticidal soap, horticultural oil or a labelled miticide, covering the undersides
Release predatory mites (e.g. Phytoseiulus persimilis) in greenhouses
prevention: Avoid drought stress and dusty conditions
Avoid broad-spectrum insecticides that kill natural predators
Inspect new plants before bringing them in

Tomato___Target_Spot.name: Target Spot
Tomato___Target_Spot.summary: A fungal disease of warm, humid regions that affects leaves, stems and fruit.
symptoms: Brown spots with light centres and faint concentric rings
Spots can merge, causing leaves to yellow and drop
Small sunken spots on fruit
treatment: Remove infected leaves and debris
Apply a labelled fungicide (e.g. chlorothalonil or azoxystrobin) when symptoms appear
prevention: Improve airflow by pruning and staking
Rotate crops and remove crop residue

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.name: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.pathogen: TYLCV (begomovirus, spread by the whitefly Bemisia tabaci)
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.summary: A devastating whitefly-transmitted virus. Plants infected young become stunted and set little or no fruit.
symptoms: Upward curling and cupping of leaves
Yellowing of leaf margins and between veins
Stunted, bushy growth and flower drop
treatment: There is no cure; remove and destroy infected plants (bag them to trap whiteflies)
Control whiteflies with yellow sticky traps, insecticidal soaps or labelled insecticides
prevention: Use insect-proof netting for seedlings and in greenhouses
Remove weeds that host whiteflies and leave a host-free period between crops

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.name: Tomato Mosaic Virus
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.summary: A very stable virus that spreads by contact: hands, tools and infected seed. It can survive in debris for long periods.
symptoms: Light and dark green mottled (mosaic) pattern on leaves
Leaf distortion, fern-like or narrowed leaves
Stunting and uneven fruit ripening
treatment: There is no cure; remove and destroy infected plants
Disinfect tools and wash hands (e.g. with milk or a disinfectant) before handling plants
prevention: Use certified virus-free or treated seed and resistant varieties
Sanitise tools, stakes and greenhouse surfaces

Tomato___healthy.name: Healthy
Tomato___healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected. The leaf looks healthy.
prevention: Mulch and water at the base
Scout lower leaves weekly for spots

Apple___Mosaic_virus.name: Apple Mosaic
Apple___Mosaic_virus.summary: A graft-transmitted virus that causes bright yellow or cream patterns on leaves. It usually reduces vigour slightly rather than killing trees.
symptoms: Bright yellow to cream blotches, rings or bands, often along veins
Patterns appear on spring leaves and may fade in summer heat
Affected leaves may scorch and drop in hot weather
treatment: There is no cure; mildly affected trees can usually stay in production
Remove severely affected trees in new plantings
prevention: Plant certified virus-free trees and rootstocks
Do not graft from symptomatic trees

Apple___Powdery_mildew.name: Powdery Mildew
Apple___Powdery_mildew.summary: A fungal disease that overwinters in buds and attacks new growth, stunting shoots and russeting fruit.
symptoms: White to grey powdery felt on young leaves and shoots
Leaves narrow, crinkle and curl upward
Silvery, stunted shoot tips that carry the fungus over winter
treatment: Prune out mildewed shoot tips in winter and during the season
Apply sulfur or another labelled fungicide from tight cluster into early summer
prevention: Avoid excess nitrogen, which drives soft, susceptible growth

Banana___Panama_disease.name: Panama Disease (Fusarium Wilt)
Banana___Panama_disease.pathogen: Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense (incl. Tropical Race 4)
Banana___Panama_disease.summary: A soil-borne wilt that blocks the plant's water-conducting tissue. The fungus survives in soil for decades, making it one of the most destructive banana diseases.
symptoms: Yellowing of older leaves, starting at the margins
Leaves collapse and hang around the pseudostem like a skirt
Splitting at the pseudostem base; red-brown streaks inside the stem
treatment: There is no cure; destroy infected plants in place and do not move soil or plant material
Report suspected TR4 to your agricultural authority where it is regulated
prevention: Use disease-free tissue-culture plantlets and tolerant cultivars
Disinfect tools, boots and vehicles between fields
Avoid moving soil and water from infested areas

Banana___healthy.name: Healthy
Banana___healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected. The leaf looks healthy.

Basil___Downy_mildew.name: Downy Mildew
Basil___Downy_mildew.summary: A fast-spreading water mould favoured by humid nights; it can ruin a basil crop within days.
symptoms: Yellowing between veins, starting on lower leaves
Grey-purple fuzzy growth on the leaf underside
Leaves turn brown and drop
treatment: Remove and bag infected plants promptly
Harvest healthy leaves early before the disease spreads
prevention: Space plants and water in the morning so leaves dry quickly
Buy seed and transplants from reliable sources

Basil___healthy.name: Healthy
Basil___healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected. The leaf looks healthy.
prevention: Water at the base in the morning
Pinch flowers to keep growth vigorous

Bean___Halo_blight.name: Halo Blight
Bean___Halo_blight.summary: A seed-borne bacterial disease favoured by cool, wet weather and spread by rain splash.
symptoms: Small water-soaked spots on leaves
A wide yellow-green halo around each spot
Greasy spots on pods; yellowing of whole plants in severe cases
treatment: Remove infected plants
Copper sprays can slow spread but will not cure infected plants
Do not work in the crop while leaves are wet
prevention: Rotate away from beans for 2 to 3 years

Bean___Mosaic_virus.name: Bean Common Mosaic
Bean___Mosaic_virus.summary: A seed-borne virus also spread by aphids. Early infections can cause large yield losses.
symptoms: Light and dark green mosaic pattern on leaves
Leaves curl downward, pucker or become distorted
Stunted plants with fewer pods
treatment: There is no cure; remove infected plants early
Control aphids around young plants

Bean___Rust.name: Bean Rust
Bean___Rust.summary: A rust disease spread by wind-blown spores in humid weather with long dew periods.
symptoms: Small reddish-brown powdery pustules, mainly on leaf undersides
Yellow halos around pustules
Leaves yellow and drop in severe cases
treatment: Apply a labelled fungicide (e.g. sulfur or chlorothalonil) at the first pustules
Remove heavily infected leaves
prevention: Rotate crops and destroy bean debris

Bean___healthy.name: Healthy
Bean___healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected. The leaf looks healthy.

Blueberry___Rust.name: Leaf Rust
Blueberry___Rust.summary: A rust disease that causes early defoliation, weakening bushes and reducing next season's crop.
symptoms: Yellow spots on the upper leaf surface that turn reddish-brown
Orange-yellow powdery pustules on the underside
Premature leaf drop late in the season
treatment: Apply a labelled fungicide when rust first appears
Remove and destroy fallen infected leaves
prevention: Keep hemlock, the alternate host, away from plantings where possible

Broccoli___Downy_mildew.name: Downy Mildew
Broccoli___Downy_mildew.summary: A water-mould disease of brassicas favoured by cool, humid conditions.
symptoms: Yellow, angular patches on the upper leaf surface
White to grey downy growth on the underside
Dark streaks in heads in severe cases
treatment: Remove infected leaves
Apply a labelled fungicide if conditions stay cool and wet
prevention: Avoid overhead watering and space plants for airflow

Broccoli___healthy.name: Healthy
Broccoli___healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected. The leaf looks healthy.

Cabbage___Alternaria_leaf_spot.name: Alternaria Leaf Spot
Cabbage___Alternaria_leaf_spot.summary: A seed-borne fungal disease of brassicas, favoured by warm, wet weather.
symptoms: Dark brown to black round spots, often with concentric rings
Yellow halo around spots; centres may drop out
Spots on heads reduce marketability
treatment: Remove lower infected leaves
Apply a labelled fungicide (e.g. chlorothalonil or azoxystrobin) when spots appear
prevention: Plough in or remove crop debris

Cabbage___healthy.name: Healthy
Cabbage___healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected. The leaf looks healthy.

Cashew___Anthracnose.name: Anthracnose
Cashew___Anthracnose.summary: A major cashew disease in humid weather, attacking young leaves, flowers and developing nuts.
symptoms: Reddish-brown to dark irregular lesions on young leaves
Lesions merge and leaves wither
Blackened flowers and shrivelled young nuts
treatment: Prune and burn infected twigs
Apply a copper-based fungicide at new flushing and flowering
prevention: Remove infected debris from under trees

Cashew___Gummosis.name: Gummosis
Cashew___Gummosis.summary: A fungal disease of the trunk and branches that causes gum oozing and can kill branches or whole trees.
symptoms: Amber gum oozing from cracks in the bark
Dark, sunken bark lesions
Yellowing leaves and dieback of affected branches
treatment: Scrape out infected bark and apply a copper-based or Bordeaux paste
Cut out and burn dead branches
prevention: Avoid wounding trunks during farm work
Keep trees vigorous with good nutrition

Cashew___Leaf_miner.name: Leaf Miner
Cashew___Leaf_miner.summary: Moth larvae tunnel inside tender young leaves, damaging new flushes.
symptoms: Silvery or whitish blister-like mines on young leaves
Mined leaves crumple, curl and dry
Damage concentrated on new flushes
treatment: Spray neem or a labelled insecticide on new flushes when mines first appear
Remove and destroy heavily mined shoots
prevention: Encourage natural enemies such as parasitic wasps

Cashew___Red_rust.name: Red Rust (Algal Leaf Spot)
Cashew___Red_rust.summary: A parasitic alga that forms rusty, velvety spots on leaves, mostly in humid, shaded conditions.
symptoms: Round, raised, orange to rust-coloured velvety spots on leaves
Spots later turn grey-green
Heavy infections weaken leaves
treatment: Apply a copper-based fungicide
Prune affected branches

Cashew___healthy.name: Healthy
Cashew___healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected. The leaf looks healthy.
prevention: Prune to keep an open canopy

Cassava___Bacterial_blight.name: Bacterial Blight
Cassava___Bacterial_blight.summary: A bacterial disease spread mainly through infected stem cuttings and rain splash. It can cause severe losses in wet seasons.
symptoms: Angular, water-soaked leaf spots that turn brown
Leaf blight and wilting
Gummy exudate on stems and shoot dieback
treatment: Uproot and burn badly infected plants
Do not take cuttings from infected fields
prevention: Plant clean cuttings from healthy fields
Rotate crops and disinfect cutting tools

Cassava___Brown_spot.name: Brown Leaf Spot
Cassava___Brown_spot.summary: A common fungal leaf spot that mostly affects older leaves and is usually of minor importance.
symptoms: Brown, angular spots with dark borders on older leaves
Spots may have a yellow halo
Older leaves yellow and drop early
treatment: Usually no treatment is needed
Remove heavily affected leaves

Cassava___Green_mite.name: Green Mite
Cassava___Green_mite.summary: A tiny mite that feeds on young leaves, especially in the dry season, and can cut yields sharply.
symptoms: Pale yellow speckling on young leaves
Leaves become small, mottled and deformed
Shoot tips look bare, like a candle-stick
treatment: Release or conserve predatory mites (e.g. Typhlodromalus aripo)
Remove and destroy badly infested shoot tips
prevention: Plant early so crops are established before the dry season
Avoid broad-spectrum insecticides that kill predators

Cassava___Mosaic_disease.name: Cassava Mosaic Disease
Cassava___Mosaic_disease.pathogen: Cassava mosaic begomoviruses (spread by whitefly and infected cuttings)
Cassava___Mosaic_disease.summary: The most damaging cassava disease in Africa. It spreads through infected stem cuttings and the whitefly Bemisia tabaci.
symptoms: Yellow-green mosaic mottling on leaves
Leaves distorted, twisted and reduced in size
Stunted plants with small roots
treatment: There is no cure; uproot and destroy infected plants early
Do not use cuttings from infected plants
prevention: Plant virus-free cuttings of resistant varieties

Cassava___healthy.name: Healthy
Cassava___healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected. The leaf looks healthy.

Cauliflower___Alternaria_leaf_spot.name: Alternaria Leaf Spot
Cauliflower___Alternaria_leaf_spot.summary: A seed-borne fungal disease of brassicas, favoured by warm, wet weather.
symptoms: Dark round spots with concentric rings on leaves
Yellow halos; spot centres may fall out
Brown spots on curds reduce quality
treatment: Remove infected lower leaves
Apply a labelled fungicide when spots appear

Cauliflower___healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected. The leaf looks healthy.

Celery___Anthracnose.name: Anthracnose (Leaf Curl)
Celery___Anthracnose.summary: A fungal disease that twists and curls celery leaves and stalks, favoured by warm, wet weather.
symptoms: Leaves cup and curl; leaf stalks twist
Tan to brown oval lesions on stalks
Distorted, stunted plants
treatment: Remove affected plants
Apply a labelled fungicide during wet periods

Celery___Early_blight.name: Early Blight
Celery___Early_blight.summary: A common fungal leaf disease of celery, spread by splashing water in warm, humid weather.
symptoms: Small yellowish spots that enlarge into grey-tan lesions
Grey fuzzy growth on lesions in humid weather
Leaves wither in severe cases
treatment: Remove infected leaves
Apply a labelled fungicide on a regular schedule in wet weather

Celery___healthy.name: Healthy
Celery___healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected. The leaf looks healthy.

Cherry___Leaf_spot.name: Cherry Leaf Spot
Cherry___Leaf_spot.summary: A common fungal disease, especially of sour cherry, that causes early defoliation and weakens trees.
symptoms: Small purple to red-brown spots on the upper leaf surface
Spot centres fall out, leaving shot holes
Leaves yellow and drop by mid-summer
treatment: Apply a labelled fungicide from petal fall through harvest in wet seasons
Rake and destroy fallen leaves
prevention: Clean up leaf litter in autumn

Citrus___Canker.name: Citrus Canker
Citrus___Canker.summary: A highly contagious bacterial disease spread by wind-driven rain, people and equipment. It is regulated in many regions.
symptoms: Raised, corky, tan-brown lesions on leaves, twigs and fruit
Water-soaked margins and a yellow halo around lesions
Lesions visible on both sides of the leaf
treatment: Report suspected cases to your agricultural authority
Remove and destroy infected shoots
Apply copper-based bactericides to protect new growth
prevention: Control citrus leaf miner, whose damage helps infection

Coffee___Leaf_rust.name: Coffee Leaf Rust
Coffee___Leaf_rust.summary: The most important coffee disease worldwide. It causes heavy leaf loss and weakens plants for the next harvest.
symptoms: Yellow-orange spots on the upper leaf surface
Orange powdery spores on the underside
Early leaf drop and branch dieback
treatment: Apply copper-based or labelled systemic fungicides at the start of the rainy season
Remove heavily infected leaves

Coffee___healthy.name: Healthy
Coffee___healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected. The leaf looks healthy.

Corn___Fall_armyworm.name: Fall Armyworm
Corn___Fall_armyworm.summary: An invasive caterpillar that feeds in the maize whorl and can destroy young crops quickly.
symptoms: Small 'windowpane' patches where young larvae scraped the leaf
Ragged holes in leaves as the whorl unfolds
Sawdust-like frass in the whorl
treatment: Scout weekly; hand-pick or crush larvae in small plots
Apply biological products (Bt, neem) or a labelled insecticide into the whorl when thresholds are reached
prevention: Plant early and at the same time as neighbours
Intercropping and push-pull systems reduce infestation

Corn___Grasshopper_damage.name: Grasshopper Damage
Corn___Grasshopper_damage.summary: Grasshoppers chew leaves from the margins; damage is usually limited unless populations are high.
symptoms: Irregular chewed areas along leaf edges
Large holes in leaves
Grasshoppers visible on plants
treatment: Light damage can usually be tolerated
Use baits or a labelled insecticide only if defoliation is severe
prevention: Manage weedy field margins where grasshoppers breed

Corn___Leaf_beetle_damage.name: Leaf Beetle Damage
Corn___Leaf_beetle_damage.summary: Adult leaf beetles scrape or chew maize leaves; some species can also spread viruses.
symptoms: Long scraped stripes or small holes in leaves
Feeding scars that turn white or brown
Beetles on leaves
treatment: Usually no treatment is needed for light damage
Apply a labelled insecticide if heavy feeding threatens young plants

Corn___Maize_streak_virus.name: Maize Streak Virus
Corn___Maize_streak_virus.pathogen: Maize streak virus (MSV, mastrevirus; spread by Cicadulina leafhoppers)
Corn___Maize_streak_virus.summary: Africa's most important maize virus. Plants infected young become stunted and may produce no grain.
symptoms: Narrow, broken yellow streaks running along leaf veins
Streaks merge into yellow stripes
Stunting when infected young
treatment: There is no cure; remove infected seedlings
Manage leafhoppers early in the season
prevention: Avoid late plantings next to older maize
Control grass weeds that host the virus

Cucumber___Angular_leaf_spot.name: Angular Leaf Spot
Cucumber___Angular_leaf_spot.summary: A seed-borne bacterial disease spread by splashing water in warm, wet weather.
symptoms: Small water-soaked spots bounded by leaf veins (angular)
Spots turn tan and dry; centres tear out
White crusty ooze on spots in the morning
treatment: Remove infected leaves
Copper sprays can slow spread

Cucumber___Bacterial_wilt.name: Bacterial Wilt
Cucumber___Bacterial_wilt.summary: A bacterial wilt spread by striped and spotted cucumber beetles. Infected plants usually die.
symptoms: Individual leaves or runners suddenly wilt
The whole plant wilts and dies
Sticky strands when a cut stem is slowly pulled apart
treatment: There is no cure; remove wilted plants
Control cucumber beetles immediately

Cucumber___Powdery_mildew.name: Powdery Mildew
Cucumber___Powdery_mildew.summary: A very common cucurbit disease that does not need wet leaves to spread.
symptoms: White powdery spots on leaves and stems
Spots spread to cover whole leaves
Leaves yellow and die early
treatment: Apply sulfur, potassium bicarbonate or another labelled fungicide early
Alternate fungicide groups to avoid resistance
prevention: Give plants full sun and airflow

Cucumber___healthy.name: Healthy
Cucumber___healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected. The leaf looks healthy.

Eggplant___Cercospora_leaf_spot.name: Cercospora Leaf Spot
Eggplant___Cercospora_leaf_spot.summary: A fungal leaf spot favoured by warm, humid weather, causing early leaf loss.
symptoms: Round to angular yellowish spots
Spots turn brown with a grey centre
Leaves yellow and drop
treatment: Remove infected leaves
Apply a labelled fungicide when spots appear

Eggplant___healthy.name: Healthy
Eggplant___healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected. The leaf looks healthy.

Garlic___Leaf_blight.name: Leaf Blight
Garlic___Leaf_blight.summary: A fungal leaf blight of garlic and onions that thrives in warm, wet weather and on stressed plants.
symptoms: Small water-soaked or yellow spots on leaves
Spots become elongated tan to brown lesions
Leaf tips die back
treatment: Remove badly affected leaves
Apply a labelled fungicide in wet weather

Garlic___Rust.name: Garlic Rust
Garlic___Rust.summary: A rust disease of garlic and leeks that reduces bulb size when infection is heavy.
symptoms: Small yellow flecks on leaves
Bright orange powdery pustules
Leaves yellow and die early
treatment: Apply a labelled fungicide at the first pustules
Remove heavily infected leaves

Garlic___healthy.name: Healthy
Garlic___healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected. The leaf looks healthy.

Ginger___Leaf_spot.name: Leaf Spot
Ginger___Leaf_spot.summary: A fungal leaf spot of ginger spread by rain splash in humid weather.
symptoms: Small oval spots with a white papery centre
Dark brown margins with a yellow halo
Spots merge and leaves dry
treatment: Remove infected leaves
Apply a labelled copper or other fungicide

Ginger___Sheath_blight.name: Sheath Blight
Ginger___Sheath_blight.summary: A soil-borne fungal disease favoured by warm, wet conditions and dense planting.
symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on leaf sheaths and leaves
Lesions with pale centres and irregular brown margins
Leaves dry from the base upward
treatment: Remove affected plants
Apply a labelled fungicide where available

Ginger___healthy.name: Healthy
Ginger___healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected. The leaf looks healthy.

Grape___Downy_mildew.name: Downy Mildew
Grape___Downy_mildew.summary: A destructive water-mould disease in warm, wet seasons that attacks leaves, shoots and clusters.
symptoms: Yellow, oily-looking spots on the upper leaf surface
White downy growth on the underside
Clusters brown and shrivel
treatment: Apply a labelled fungicide (e.g. copper or mancozeb) before and during wet periods
Remove infected shoots and clusters

Grape___Leafroll_disease.name: Leafroll Disease
Grape___Leafroll_disease.summary: A virus disease spread by infected planting material and mealybugs. It lowers yield and delays ripening.
symptoms: Leaves roll downward in late summer
Red or purple leaves with green veins (red varieties)
Yellowing between veins (white varieties)
treatment: There is no cure; remove infected vines
Control mealybugs to limit spread

Lettuce___Downy_mildew.name: Downy Mildew
Lettuce___Downy_mildew.summary: A water-mould disease favoured by cool, moist conditions.
symptoms: Pale yellow, angular patches on older leaves
White downy growth on the underside
Patches turn brown and dry
treatment: Remove infected leaves
Apply a labelled fungicide in cool, wet weather

Lettuce___Mosaic_virus.name: Lettuce Mosaic
Lettuce___Mosaic_virus.summary: A seed-borne virus spread further by aphids.
symptoms: Mottling and vein clearing on leaves
Leaves ruffled or distorted
Stunting; heads fail to form
treatment: There is no cure; remove infected plants
Control aphids
prevention: Control weeds that host the virus
Avoid planting next to old lettuce crops

Lettuce___healthy.name: Healthy
Lettuce___healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected. The leaf looks healthy.

Maple___Tar_spot.name: Tar Spot
Maple___Tar_spot.summary: A mostly cosmetic leaf disease of maples that rarely harms tree health.
symptoms: Yellow-green spots in early summer
Spots develop raised, shiny black 'tar' patches
Possible early leaf drop
treatment: Usually no treatment is needed

Maple___healthy.name: Healthy
Maple___healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected. The leaf looks healthy.

Peach___Leaf_curl.name: Peach Leaf Curl
Peach___Leaf_curl.summary: A fungal disease that infects buds in late winter and distorts spring leaves.
symptoms: Thickened, puckered, curled leaves
Leaves turn red, purple or yellow
Infected leaves drop early
treatment: Once symptoms appear, spraying will not help this season
Remove distorted leaves and support the tree with water and nutrition
prevention: Apply one fungicide spray (e.g. copper or chlorothalonil) after leaf fall or before bud swell

Plum___Pocket_disease.name: Plum Pocket
Plum___Pocket_disease.summary: A fungal disease that turns young plums into swollen, hollow, deformed 'bladders'.
symptoms: Swollen, hollow, distorted fruit
Fruit surface turns grey and powdery
Thickened, curled leaves and shoots
treatment: Remove and destroy infected fruit and shoots
prevention: Apply a dormant fungicide spray before bud swell

Plum___healthy.name: Healthy
Plum___healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected. The leaf looks healthy.

Rice___Blast.name: Rice Blast
Rice___Blast.summary: One of the most destructive rice diseases worldwide. It attacks leaves, nodes and panicles.
symptoms: Diamond or spindle-shaped lesions with grey centres and brown margins
Lesions merge and leaves die
Neck rot that makes panicles break or stay empty
treatment: Apply a labelled fungicide (e.g. tricyclazole or azoxystrobin) at early symptoms or booting
Avoid excess nitrogen

Rice___Sheath_blight.name: Sheath Blight
Rice___Sheath_blight.summary: A soil-borne disease favoured by dense crops, high nitrogen and warm, humid conditions.
symptoms: Oval, greenish-grey lesions on sheaths near the water line
Lesions turn pale with brown borders
The disease climbs to upper leaves
treatment: Apply a labelled fungicide (e.g. validamycin or azoxystrobin) when lesions are found

Rice___healthy.name: Healthy
Rice___healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected. The leaf looks healthy.

Squash___Zucchini_yellow_mosaic_virus.name: Zucchini Yellow Mosaic
Squash___Zucchini_yellow_mosaic_virus.summary: An aphid-transmitted virus that can make a whole crop unmarketable.
symptoms: Yellow mosaic and vein clearing on leaves
Leaves narrow, blistered and distorted
Knobby, deformed fruit
treatment: There is no cure; remove infected plants early
Control aphids
prevention: Use reflective mulch or row covers early

Squash___healthy.name: Healthy
Squash___healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected. The leaf looks healthy.

Strawberry___Anthracnose.name: Anthracnose
Strawberry___Anthracnose.summary: A fungal disease spread by infected plants and splashing water, attacking fruit, crowns and leaves.
symptoms: Dark sunken spots on fruit with orange spore masses
Black spots on leaves and runners
Crown rot that makes plants wilt
treatment: Remove infected plants and fruit
Apply a labelled fungicide during wet weather
prevention: Use drip irrigation and straw mulch

Tobacco___Mosaic_virus.name: Tobacco Mosaic
Tobacco___Mosaic_virus.summary: A very stable virus spread by contact: hands, tools and infected plant debris.
symptoms: Light and dark green mosaic pattern
Leaf puckering and distortion
Stunted growth
treatment: There is no cure; remove infected plants
Wash hands and disinfect tools
prevention: Avoid handling plants after using tobacco products

Tobacco___healthy.name: Healthy
Tobacco___healthy.summary: No disease symptoms detected. The leaf looks healthy.

Tomato___Verticillium_wilt.name: Verticillium Wilt
Tomato___Verticillium_wilt.summary: A soil-borne wilt fungus that survives in soil for years and blocks the plant's water-conducting tissue.
symptoms: V-shaped yellow patches on lower leaves
Wilting during the hottest part of the day
Brown streaks inside the lower stem
treatment: There is no chemical cure; remove infected plants
Keep plants watered to reduce stress
prevention: Rotate away from solanaceous crops for several years
